title: Slow-Simmered Dulce de Leche
summary: Silky homemade dulce de leche simmered gently from whole milk and sugar until deep caramel brown and thick enough to spread.

steps.title: Dissolve the sugar
steps.text: Combine the milk and sugar in the large pan over medium heat and stir occasionally until the sugar has dissolved and the milk barely simmers. A wide, heavy pan gives a gentle, even heat and room for the milk to foam.

steps.title: Add the bicarbonate
steps.text: Lift the pan off the heat and stir in the bicarbonate of soda. The milk will bubble up vigorously; keep stirring until it calms. The bicarbonate speeds the browning and helps keep the milk proteins from turning grainy.

steps.title: Simmer slowly
steps.text: Put the pan back over the lowest possible heat and let it cook uncovered at the gentlest simmer for 2.5-3 h. Stir every 10-15 min, scraping the base, and more often during the last 30 min as it thickens; leave the foam on the surface alone.

steps.title: Check for doneness
steps.text: It is ready once it is a deep caramel brown, has reduced to about 300 g and coats the back of a spoon in a thick layer. Remember it firms up considerably as it cools.

steps.title: Strain and store
steps.text: Pour it through the fine sieve into the bowl while hot, stir in the vanilla and leave to cool. Spoon into a clean jar and cover.

tips: The most common mistake is turning up the heat to save time; the milk scorches on the base and turns bitter, so keep it at a bare simmer.
Use a pan holding at least 4 litres; the milk foams up when the bicarbonate goes in.
If it sets too thick once cold, warm it gently with a spoonful of milk.
Stop a little earlier for a pourable sauce, or cook longer for a firm spread.
storage: Keep in a covered jar in the fridge for up to 3 weeks. Bring to room temperature or warm gently before using.
